questions.stem: Ifeoma's mother returns excess change to a market woman who gave her too much money. The value displayed is
questions.explanation: Returning money that does not belong to you shows honesty.

questions.stem: Members of a community contribute money and labour to repair a bridge washed away by flood. This shows the value of
questions.explanation: Cooperation means working together with others towards a common goal.

questions.stem: Which of the following agents plays the earliest role in passing values to a child?
questions.explanation: The family is the first agent of socialisation, where a child first learns right from wrong.

questions.stem: A student who completes his assignment on time without being reminded by the teacher shows
questions.explanation: Self-discipline is the ability to control oneself and do what is required without external pressure.

questions.stem: A Muslim student and a Christian student share a desk and respect each other's religious practices. This illustrates
questions.explanation: Tolerance is accepting and respecting beliefs and practices different from one's own.

questions.stem: The value of justice requires that
options: leaders should favour their relatives and friends when sharing public offices
everyone is treated fairly according to the rules
offenders should be punished without trial
only the rich should receive protection
the majority may oppress the minority
questions.explanation: Justice means fair and equal treatment of all persons in accordance with established rules.

questions.stem: Which of the following is likely to result when a society neglects the value of dignity of labour?
options: More people will go into farming and crafts
Corruption in public offices will disappear
Productivity in all sectors will rise sharply
There will be less demand for white-collar jobs
Youths may prefer quick money to honest work
questions.explanation: When honest manual work is despised, young people may chase quick wealth through crime or fraud.

questions.stem: A society that rewards wealth without asking how it was acquired is most likely to encourage
options: respect for the rule of law
questions.explanation: Celebrating wealth regardless of its source encourages people to acquire it by any means, including corruption.

questions.stem: The National Orientation Agency was established mainly to
options: conduct elections into all public offices and announce the official results
promote positive values and enlighten citizens on government programmes
questions.explanation: The NOA mobilises and educates citizens, promotes national values and explains government policies.

questions.stem: A person who is satisfied with what he earns legitimately and does not envy others is said to be
questions.explanation: Contentment is satisfaction with one's lawful possessions and achievements.

questions.stem: A girl reports a classmate who is bullying younger students even though the bully has threatened her. She has shown
questions.explanation: Courage is the ability to do what is right despite fear or threat.

questions.stem: Which of the following best explains why values differ from one society to another?
options: Values are fixed by the United Nations and imposed on every member country
Values are determined by the weather of a place
Values are inherited biologically from parents
Societies have different cultures, religions and experiences
questions.explanation: Values are shaped by culture, religion, history and environment, so they vary across societies.

questions.stem: The two horses on the Nigerian coat of arms represent
questions.explanation: The horses stand for dignity; the eagle represents strength and the black shield fertile soil.

questions.stem: The national flower shown at the base of the Nigerian coat of arms is the
questions.explanation: The yellow Costus spectabilis is Nigeria's national flower and appears at the base of the coat of arms.

questions.stem: The black shield on the Nigerian coat of arms stands for
options: the colour of the nation's people
mourning for past leaders who died while in office
questions.explanation: The black shield represents Nigeria's fertile soil.

questions.stem: The Nigerian national flag was designed by
questions.explanation: Taiwo Akinkunmi designed the green-white-green flag in 1959 while a student in London.

questions.stem: The words of the Nigerian national pledge were written by
questions.explanation: Professor Felicia Adeyoyin wrote the national pledge in 1976.

questions.stem: The anthem "Nigeria, We Hail Thee", restored as Nigeria's national anthem in 2024, was first adopted at
options: the end of the civil war in 1970
the return to civil rule in 1979
the start of the Fourth Republic in 1999
questions.explanation: The anthem was first used from independence in 1960 until 1978, and was restored in 2024.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a national symbol of Nigeria?
questions.explanation: A party logo belongs to a political party, not to the nation as a whole.

questions.stem: The difference between nationalism and patriotism is that nationalism
options: often involves the struggle for self-rule or national identity, while patriotism is love and loyalty to one's country
is a duty of citizens while patriotism is merely a right that citizens may choose to enjoy or ignore entirely
applies only to soldiers while patriotism applies to civilians
is required by law while patriotism is forbidden by law
is practised only after independence while patriotism ended with colonial rule
questions.explanation: Nationalism stresses national identity and, historically, the struggle for independence; patriotism is devotion and loyalty to one's country.

questions.stem: A Lagos-born corps member serving in Sokoto learns Hausa, celebrates Sallah with his host family and starts a free evening class. This experience best reflects which objective of the NYSC?
options: Training youths for the armed forces
Providing cheap labour for private firms
Reducing the number of university graduates
questions.explanation: The NYSC was set up in 1973 to foster unity by posting graduates to states other than their own.

questions.stem: The identification number issued to every Nigerian and legal resident by the National Identity Management Commission is the
options: Bank Verification Number for account holders
questions.explanation: The NIMC issues the National Identification Number (NIN) for identity management.

questions.stem: Nigeria celebrates its Independence Day on
questions.explanation: Nigeria became independent on 1 October 1960.

questions.stem: Rights which every person enjoys simply because he or she is a human being are called
questions.explanation: Human rights are inherent entitlements of every human being.

questions.stem: A lawyer preparing to defend a client’s right to fair hearing would turn to which part of the 1999 Constitution?
questions.explanation: Chapter IV (sections 33 to 46) contains fundamental rights.

questions.stem: The Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy in Chapter II of the 1999 Constitution are generally
questions.explanation: Section 6(6)(c) provides that the courts generally cannot enforce Chapter II objectives.

questions.stem: Which of the following rights is classified as an economic, social and cultural right?
questions.explanation: Education is a socio-economic right; voting, fair hearing, expression and life are civil and political rights.

questions.stem: A person who believes that his fundamental right has been violated may apply for redress to the
questions.explanation: Section 46 gives the High Court special jurisdiction to enforce fundamental rights.

questions.stem: Under section 45 of the 1999 Constitution, certain fundamental rights may be restricted by law in the interest of
options: the ruling party at election time, as decided by its national chairman
defence, public safety, public order, public morality or public health
any public officer who so wishes
the personal convenience of the police
questions.explanation: Section 45 permits laws reasonably justifiable in a democratic society in the interest of defence, public safety, order, morality or health, or to protect the rights of others.

questions.stem: A police officer beats a suspect to obtain a confession. Which right has been violated most directly?
options: Freedom of movement within and out of Nigeria
Right to dignity of the human person
questions.explanation: Section 34 protects dignity and forbids torture and inhuman or degrading treatment.

questions.stem: Which of the following laws was enacted in Nigeria in 2015 to prohibit violence such as rape, female genital mutilation and domestic violence?
options: Cybercrimes (Prohibition, Prevention, etc.) Act of the National Assembly
questions.explanation: The Violence Against Persons (Prohibition) Act 2015 criminalises many forms of violence, especially against women and girls.

questions.stem: The right to vote and to be voted for is an example of
questions.explanation: Political rights relate to participation in government, such as voting and standing for election.

questions.stem: Fatima, who uses a wheelchair, cannot enter a public hospital because it has only stairs. A Nigerian law that addresses this situation is the
options: Discrimination Against Persons with Disabilities (Prohibition) Act
Federal Road Safety Commission (Establishment) Act of 2007
questions.explanation: The Discrimination Against Persons with Disabilities (Prohibition) Act requires public buildings to be made accessible and prohibits discrimination.

questions.stem: A law made by the National Assembly or a State House of Assembly is called
questions.explanation: Statutes are laws passed by a legislature.

questions.stem: The main purpose of law in society is to
options: make the rich richer and protect only those in power
questions.explanation: Laws set standards of conduct and help keep peace and order.

questions.stem: A law dealing with offences against the state such as armed robbery and murder is
questions.explanation: Criminal law concerns wrongs against society, prosecuted by the state.

questions.stem: Mr Ade sues his neighbour for building a fence on his land. This case falls under
questions.explanation: Disputes between private persons over land or contracts are civil matters.

questions.stem: The Nigerian law of 2015 that introduced non-custodial sentences such as community service for some offences is the
questions.explanation: The Administration of Criminal Justice Act 2015 reformed criminal procedure and provided for non-custodial sentences.

questions.stem: The paramilitary agency that protects critical national infrastructure such as pipelines and assists in maintaining internal security is the
options: Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps
Nigeria Immigration Service and its border patrol units
questions.explanation: The NSCDC protects public infrastructure and supports internal security.

questions.stem: A mob beats a suspected phone thief to death without trial. This act violates the principle that
options: laws are made by the legislature
every accused person is presumed innocent until proven guilty
courts are independent of the executive arm of government
only the police can enforce traffic rules
questions.explanation: Section 36(5) presumes every accused innocent until proven guilty; jungle justice denies fair hearing and the right to life.

questions.stem: Which of the following best explains why law and order is necessary for economic development?
options: Law and order increases the number of public holidays
Investors prefer a secure environment where contracts are respected
Law and order reduces the need for schools
Disorder attracts foreign investors who prefer to take risks in unstable places
Law and order makes taxation unnecessary
questions.explanation: Security of lives and property and enforceable contracts encourage investment and trade.

questions.stem: The nationwide toll-free emergency telephone number in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: 112 is the national emergency number for police, fire and ambulance services.

questions.stem: Parents who plan the number of children they can adequately cater for are practising
questions.explanation: Family planning enables couples to decide the number and spacing of their children.

questions.stem: Under the Child's Rights Act 2003, a child is a person below the age of
questions.explanation: The Act defines a child as a person who has not attained 18 years.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of child neglect?
options: Sending a child to school regularly
Correcting a child gently but firmly whenever he does wrong at home
Failing to provide a child with food and medical care
Spending time with a child after school
questions.explanation: Neglect is failure to meet a child's basic needs such as food, health care and education.

questions.stem: The registration of a newborn baby's birth in Nigeria is handled by the
questions.explanation: The National Population Commission keeps the register of births and deaths.

questions.stem: A couple sends their 12-year-old daughter to hawk on the highway during school hours. This practice exposes the child mainly to
options: exploitation, accidents and loss of education
improved family planning and better feeding in the home
questions.explanation: Child hawking exposes children to road accidents, abuse and trafficking and keeps them out of school.

questions.stem: Health workers advise mothers to feed their babies only on breast milk for the first
questions.explanation: Exclusive breastfeeding for six months is recommended for the healthy growth of infants.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most likely consequence of irresponsible parenthood on society?
options: Reduction in crime among young people
Improvement in school enrolment and in the academic performance of pupils
Increase in juvenile delinquency and street children
Decline in the number of out-of-school children
questions.explanation: Children deprived of care and guidance are more likely to drift into crime and street life.

questions.stem: A road sign that is rectangular in shape usually
options: gives a warning of danger ahead
orders drivers to stop at once
commands drivers to turn left only
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs are informative, e.g. directions and distances.

questions.stem: Which of the following road users should use the zebra crossing?
questions.explanation: The zebra crossing is a marked crossing point for pedestrians.

questions.stem: An inverted triangular sign with a red border at a junction instructs a driver to
options: increase speed to clear the junction
give way to traffic on the main road
park on the left side of the road
stop and switch off the engine
questions.explanation: The inverted triangle is the "give way" (yield) sign.

questions.stem: A circular road sign with a blue background usually indicates
options: a warning of a sharp bend
the distance to the next town
questions.explanation: Blue circular signs give mandatory instructions, such as "keep left".

questions.stem: The Federal Road Safety Commission was established in
questions.explanation: The FRSC was established in 1988; its current establishing Act was passed in 2007.

questions.stem: Musa drives while pressing his phone to read messages. The main danger of this habit is that it
options: distracts him and slows his reaction time
makes the vehicle consume more fuel on long journeys between cities
improves his concentration on the road
reduces the noise in the vehicle
questions.explanation: Using a phone while driving diverts attention and is a major cause of crashes; it is a traffic offence.

questions.stem: Which of the following documents shows that a vehicle has been inspected and found fit to be used on the road?
options: Tax clearance certificate of the vehicle owner
questions.explanation: The roadworthiness certificate is issued after a vehicle passes inspection.

questions.stem: Speed limiting devices were made compulsory by the FRSC mainly for
questions.explanation: The FRSC directed commercial vehicles to install speed limiters to reduce crashes caused by over-speeding.

questions.stem: A pedestrian walking along a highway where there is no footpath should walk
options: with his back to the traffic
in the middle of the road
questions.explanation: Facing oncoming traffic lets the pedestrian see vehicles approaching and react.

questions.stem: The wearing of seat belts by drivers and passengers in front seats helps to
questions.explanation: Seat belts restrain occupants and reduce injuries and deaths in crashes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the BEST explanation for why overloading a vehicle causes accidents?
options: It makes the vehicle lighter and therefore harder for the driver to steer
It increases the brightness of headlamps
It reduces the speed of the vehicle to zero
It reduces the driver's control and makes braking less effective
It makes the road surface smoother
questions.explanation: Extra weight lengthens stopping distance, strains tyres and brakes and makes the vehicle unstable.

questions.stem: Traffic wardens and officers who control traffic within Lagos State are members of the
questions.explanation: LASTMA manages traffic in Lagos State; the FRSC operates mainly on highways nationwide.

questions.stem: The relationship between a teacher and her students is an example of
questions.explanation: Teacher-student relationships are formal, governed by rules and roles.

questions.stem: Listening carefully to understand what another person is saying is called
questions.explanation: Active listening involves giving full attention and responding appropriately.

questions.stem: When a neutral third party helps two quarrelling neighbours reach their own agreement, the method used is
questions.explanation: A mediator assists the parties to reach a settlement but does not impose a decision.

questions.stem: In arbitration, the third party
options: only carries messages between the parties without ever expressing any view of the dispute
punishes the party who started the quarrel
takes the side of the more powerful party
refuses to listen to evidence from either side
hears both sides and gives a decision that the parties agree to accept
questions.explanation: An arbitrator, chosen by the parties, hears both sides and makes an award.

questions.stem: Chidi often borrows money from friends and never pays back. This attitude is likely to
options: make his friends trust him more
earn him the respect of his classmates
questions.explanation: Dishonesty and failure to keep promises damage trust in relationships.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a feature of a healthy friendship?
questions.explanation: Healthy friendships are built on respect, trust, honesty and good communication.

questions.stem: Repeatedly intimidating, mocking or hurting a weaker student, in person or online, is known as
questions.explanation: Bullying is the repeated use of power to harm or intimidate a weaker person, including cyberbullying.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about conflict in inter-personal relationships is MOST accurate?
options: Well-managed conflict can lead to better understanding
All conflicts must end in violence unless the police intervene early
Conflict can never be resolved peacefully
Conflict is always caused by poverty
questions.explanation: Conflict is normal; handled properly through dialogue it can improve understanding and relationships.

questions.stem: Seeing a problem from another person's point of view and sharing his feelings is
questions.explanation: Empathy is the ability to understand and share the feelings of another.

questions.stem: Which of the following words helps to build good relationships?
questions.explanation: Courtesy expressions such as "thank you" and "please" promote good relationships.

questions.stem: A secret group whose members swear oaths of loyalty and often use violence to settle scores is a
questions.explanation: Secret cults are characterised by secret oaths, initiation rites and violence.

questions.stem: The first known campus confraternity in Nigeria, the Pyrates Confraternity, was founded in the early 1950s at
questions.explanation: The Pyrates Confraternity was founded at University College, Ibadan, by Wole Soyinka and six others; it was not formed as a violent cult.

questions.stem: Section 38(4) of the 1999 Constitution provides that the right to freedom of thought, conscience and religion does NOT entitle anyone to
options: take part in the activities of a secret society
teach his religion to his children
questions.explanation: Section 38(4) excludes membership of or participation in secret societies from the protection of section 38.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a sign that a student may have been initiated into a cult?
options: Sudden secretive behaviour and unusual new friends
Improved performance in examinations and tests across all subjects
Willingness to share his problems openly
questions.explanation: Secrecy, unexplained absences, new dangerous associates and aggression may indicate cult membership.

questions.stem: A major reason why some students join secret cults is the desire for
options: protection and a sense of belonging
questions.explanation: Students may join cults seeking protection, power, belonging or a means to settle grievances.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most effective long-term way to reduce cultism in Nigerian schools?
options: Allowing cults to operate openly on campuses
Abolishing all student clubs, societies and associations in every school in the country
Providing counselling, recreation and strict enforcement of anti-cult rules
Expelling every student who keeps friends
Closing all universities for several years
questions.explanation: Guidance and counselling, healthy alternative activities and firm enforcement of rules address the causes and deter membership.

questions.stem: Cult clashes in a community are likely to have all the following effects EXCEPT
options: an increase in investment and peaceful trade
questions.explanation: Violence discourages investment and trade rather than increasing it.

questions.stem: Bimpe is told she must join a group of "sisters" at night in the bush and swear an oath of secrecy. The best thing for her to do is to
options: keep the matter secret to protect herself from the threats of the group
tell other students to join with her
refuse and report to her parents or school authorities
questions.explanation: Refusing and reporting to trusted adults protects her and helps authorities act.

questions.stem: Cultism in schools mostly thrives because of
questions.explanation: Cults depend on secrecy, which makes them difficult to detect.

questions.stem: The role of parents in preventing cultism includes
options: giving children unlimited pocket money so that they will not be tempted
encouraging children to settle scores by force
ignoring changes in their children's behaviour
monitoring the friends and activities of their children
discouraging children from talking to teachers
questions.explanation: Parental monitoring, guidance and good examples reduce the risk of children joining cults.

questions.stem: Students who join cults are likely to face which of the following consequences under school rules and the law?
options: Automatic promotion to the next class
questions.explanation: Cult membership attracts expulsion from school and prosecution under state anti-cult laws.

questions.stem: A substance that changes the way the body or mind works when taken is a
questions.explanation: A drug is any substance that alters the functioning of the body or mind.

questions.stem: Alcohol and sleeping pills such as barbiturates are classified as
questions.explanation: Depressants slow down the activity of the central nervous system.

questions.stem: Drugs such as LSD that cause a person to see or hear things that do not exist are called
questions.explanation: Hallucinogens distort perception and cause hallucinations.

questions.stem: When a drug user needs larger and larger doses of a drug to get the same effect, he has developed
questions.explanation: Tolerance develops when the body adapts to a drug so that more is needed for the same effect.

questions.stem: The unpleasant physical and mental symptoms that occur when a dependent person suddenly stops taking a drug are called
questions.explanation: Withdrawal symptoms such as shaking, sweating and anxiety occur when a drug of dependence is stopped.

questions.stem: Tramadol, often misused by some Nigerian youths, belongs to the group of drugs known as
questions.explanation: Tramadol is an opioid analgesic; misuse can lead to dependence, seizures and death.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the main difference between drug use and drug abuse?
options: Drug use is always illegal while drug abuse is legal when done in private at home
Drug abuse is the use of a drug in a way or quantity not medically prescribed
Drug abuse refers only to the use of injections
Drug use applies only to hard drugs
There is no difference between the two terms
questions.explanation: Drug use for medical purposes as prescribed is acceptable; abuse is non-medical or excessive use that harms the user.

questions.stem: A trader displays tablets without labels and sells them to anyone who asks. The agency that should seize these unregistered drugs is
questions.explanation: NAFDAC regulates the manufacture, importation, distribution and sale of drugs and seizes unregistered products.

questions.stem: Which of the following can lead a youth into drug abuse?
questions.explanation: Peer pressure and bad company are major causes of drug abuse among young people.

questions.stem: Drug abuse contributes to insecurity in society mainly because
options: drugs make people too weak and sleepy to commit any crime against their neighbours
drug users are always arrested before they act
drugs improve the judgement of users
drug users are protected by law
users may commit crimes to obtain money for drugs or while under their influence
questions.explanation: Drug abuse is linked with crimes such as stealing, robbery and violence.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a legal stimulant commonly found in coffee and kola nut?
questions.explanation: Caffeine is a mild stimulant found in coffee, tea and kola nut.

questions.stem: A rehabilitation centre helps a drug addict mainly by
options: treating and counselling him to stop drug use and return to normal life
keeping him away from his family and friends permanently in a locked cell
teaching him how to sell drugs safely
questions.explanation: Rehabilitation combines treatment, counselling and skills training to help addicts recover.

questions.stem: The recruitment, transport or harbouring of persons by deception or force for the purpose of exploitation is
questions.explanation: Human trafficking involves moving or keeping people by force, fraud or deception to exploit them.

questions.stem: The Nigerian agency against human trafficking, NAPTIP, was established in
questions.explanation: NAPTIP was created under the Trafficking in Persons (Prohibition) Law Enforcement and Administration Act of 2003.

questions.stem: Forcing a trafficked child to work long hours as a house help without pay is an example of
questions.explanation: Domestic servitude is a form of forced labour common in child trafficking.

questions.stem: Which of the following groups is most vulnerable to human trafficking?
options: Senior government officials and their aides
questions.explanation: Poverty, ignorance and unemployment make young people easy targets for traffickers.

questions.stem: The illegal removal and sale of human organs such as kidneys after luring victims is known as
questions.explanation: Organ harvesting is a form of exploitation linked to human trafficking.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT usually a sign that a person may be a victim of trafficking?
options: Being afraid to speak to strangers or the police
Holding his own passport and moving freely
Owing a large debt to an employer
questions.explanation: Victims usually have their documents seized and their movement controlled; holding one's own passport and moving freely is not a sign.

questions.stem: The United Nations protocol of 2000 that commits states to prevent and punish trafficking in persons, especially women and children, is commonly called the
questions.explanation: The Palermo Protocol supplements the UN Convention against Transnational Organised Crime.

questions.stem: Victims of trafficking for sexual exploitation may suffer
options: legal residence in the destination country
questions.explanation: Victims face abuse, disease, psychological trauma and sometimes death.

questions.stem: Which of the following can help reduce human trafficking in Nigeria?
options: Encouraging parents to give out their children to distant relatives in big cities
Public enlightenment on the tricks of traffickers
questions.explanation: Awareness campaigns help families recognise and resist traffickers.

questions.stem: Recruiters who promise young girls jobs abroad and then force them into prostitution mainly use
questions.explanation: Traffickers commonly lure victims with false promises of jobs or education.

questions.stem: Children used as fighters by armed groups are victims of
questions.explanation: Recruitment of children by armed groups is a form of trafficking and a grave violation of children's rights.

questions.stem: The virus that causes AIDS mainly destroys cells of the
questions.explanation: HIV attacks CD4 cells of the immune system, weakening the body's defence.

questions.stem: HIV cannot be transmitted by
options: sharing a classroom or shaking hands
unprotected sexual intercourse with an infected person
questions.explanation: HIV is not spread by casual contact such as shaking hands or sharing classrooms.

questions.stem: The period after infection when an HIV test may not yet detect the virus is called the
questions.explanation: During the window period antibodies are not yet detectable even though the person can transmit the virus.

questions.stem: The Nigerian agency that coordinates the national response to HIV and AIDS is the
options: National Emergency Management Agency and its state offices
National Agency for the Control of AIDS
questions.explanation: NACA coordinates the national multisectoral response to HIV/AIDS.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the safest way for an unmarried young person to avoid sexual transmission of HIV?
questions.explanation: Abstinence from sex removes the risk of sexual transmission.

questions.stem: Antiretroviral therapy helps people living with HIV mainly by
options: completely removing the virus from the body after a few months of treatment
suppressing the virus so that they can live long and healthy lives
replacing the need for any medical care
questions.explanation: ART reduces viral load and allows the immune system to recover, but it does not cure HIV.

questions.stem: A law passed in Nigeria in 2014 to protect people living with HIV from discrimination at work and in public places is the
questions.explanation: The HIV and AIDS (Anti-Discrimination) Act 2014 protects the rights of people living with HIV.

questions.stem: HIV counselling and testing is important because it
options: spreads the virus to other people
guarantees that the person tested will never be infected in future
is a punishment for infected persons
helps people know their status and seek early care
questions.explanation: Knowing one's status allows early treatment and prevention of further spread.

questions.stem: Sharing which of the following items can spread HIV?
questions.explanation: Razor blades and needles can carry infected blood; plates and toilet seats do not transmit HIV.

questions.stem: A student refuses to sit beside a classmate known to be living with HIV. This attitude is
questions.explanation: Stigmatisation is negative treatment of people because of their HIV status.

questions.stem: Which of the following best explains why stigma hinders the control of HIV?
options: Stigma kills the virus in the body
Stigma encourages people to disclose their status openly to their friends
People avoid testing and treatment for fear of rejection
questions.explanation: Fear of discrimination discourages testing, disclosure and treatment, allowing the virus to spread.

questions.stem: HIV is a type of
questions.explanation: HIV is a retrovirus.

questions.stem: Teaching young people practical skills such as tailoring and phone repair so that they can earn a living is an aspect of
questions.explanation: Youth empowerment equips young people with skills, resources and opportunities to be self-reliant.

questions.stem: The skills acquisition and entrepreneurship programme run for corps members during the service year is known as
questions.explanation: The NYSC Skills Acquisition and Entrepreneurship Development (SAED) programme trains corps members in vocational and business skills.

questions.stem: The federal government programme launched in 2016 that engaged unemployed graduates and non-graduates as teaching, health and agricultural assistants was
questions.explanation: N-Power, under the National Social Investment Programme, placed young people in volunteer jobs with monthly stipends.

questions.stem: The Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), set up in 2024, is meant to help students by
options: giving free cars and houses to graduates after their service year
providing interest-free loans for tertiary education
questions.explanation: NELFUND provides interest-free loans for tuition and upkeep to eligible students in tertiary institutions.

questions.stem: The Students Industrial Work Experience Scheme (SIWES) is managed by the
questions.explanation: The ITF manages SIWES, which gives students practical industrial experience.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most likely consequence of high youth unemployment in a country?
options: Fall in the rate of rural-urban migration
Reduction in the number of street hawkers
Increase in crime and youth restiveness
Increase in tax revenue from young people
questions.explanation: Idle and frustrated youths may be drawn into crime, cultism, drug abuse and violent agitation.

questions.stem: Kemi has a small bead-making business but cannot expand because she lacks capital. Which body is set up specifically to support small businesses like hers?
options: Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria
Nigerian Communications Commission and its regional offices
questions.explanation: SMEDAN supports micro, small and medium enterprises with training, advice and access to finance.

questions.stem: Many beneficiaries of a state skills scheme never received their starter packs because officials diverted the funds. This illustrates which problem of youth empowerment schemes?
options: too many jobs available for youths
lack of interest by all young people
excessive monitoring by the government of every beneficiary
questions.explanation: Inadequate funding, corruption, political interference and poor monitoring weaken many programmes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a vocational skill that can make a youth self-employed?
questions.explanation: Fashion design is a legitimate trade; the others are vices or crimes.

questions.stem: Youth empowerment benefits the nation mainly by
options: reducing the number of skilled workers
encouraging dependence on government handouts and political patrons
questions.explanation: Empowered youths become productive, create jobs and contribute to economic growth.

questions.stem: A secondary school graduate who learns to install and repair solar systems and later trains apprentices is contributing to national development mainly through
questions.explanation: Self-employment that trains others creates jobs and spreads useful skills.

questions.stem: Lack of access to start-up capital for youths can be addressed through
questions.explanation: Soft loans and grants make it easier for young people to start businesses.

questions.stem: In Nigeria, the chief executive of a local government council is the
questions.explanation: The elected chairman heads the executive of the local government council.

questions.stem: The law-making body at the local government level in Nigeria is made up of the
questions.explanation: Elected councillors form the legislative arm of the local government council and make bye-laws.

questions.stem: In a Nigerian state, commissioners are appointed by the governor subject to confirmation by the
questions.explanation: Section 192 requires House of Assembly confirmation of nominees for commissioner.

questions.stem: Under the 1999 Constitution, the President must appoint at least one minister from
options: each geopolitical zone only, as rotated by the ruling party
questions.explanation: Section 147(3) requires at least one minister from each state who is an indigene of that state.

questions.stem: The head of the judiciary in a Nigerian state is the
questions.explanation: The Chief Judge heads the State High Court and the state judiciary.

questions.stem: The minimum age for election as a member of a State House of Assembly under the 1999 Constitution (as amended) is
questions.explanation: The Not Too Young To Run amendment of 2018 reduced the age from 30 to 25 years.

questions.stem: To remove a state governor through impeachment, the House of Assembly must, after an investigation panel finds the allegations proved, adopt the report by a resolution of not less than
options: three-quarters of the people of the state
a simple majority of members present
questions.explanation: Section 188 requires adoption by not less than two-thirds of all the members of the House of Assembly.

questions.stem: The investigation panel in the impeachment of a governor is appointed by the
options: Speaker of the House of Representatives
questions.explanation: Section 188(5) provides that the Chief Judge of the state appoints a panel of seven persons to investigate the allegations.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an advisory body to the President that includes former Presidents, former Chief Justices and state governors?
questions.explanation: The Council of State advises the President on matters such as the census, prerogative of mercy and national honours.

questions.stem: The symbol of authority of a legislative house in Nigeria, without which it cannot sit lawfully, is the
questions.explanation: The mace is the symbol of the authority of the legislature.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of the judiciary that serves as a check on the executive?
options: Approving the national budget and supplementary appropriation bills
Declaring unconstitutional executive actions null and void
questions.explanation: Through judicial review the courts nullify executive acts that violate the constitution or law.

questions.stem: The second-in-command to the governor of a state is the
questions.explanation: The deputy governor is elected on the same ticket as the governor and deputises for him.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem: Abraham Lincoln defined democracy as government of the people, by the people and
questions.explanation: Lincoln described democracy as government of the people, by the people, for the people.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem: Ancient Athens practised a form of democracy in which citizens met together to make decisions. This is called
questions.explanation: In direct democracy citizens personally take part in making decisions.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem: The principle that the decision of the majority should prevail while the rights of the minority are protected is a feature of
questions.explanation: Majority rule with minority rights is a basic principle of democracy.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem: The Human Development Index used by the United Nations to measure development combines income per head, education and
questions.explanation: The HDI combines life expectancy, education and income per person.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem: Nigeria and other UN member states set themselves seventeen global goals, covering poverty, education and climate, with a deadline in the year
questions.explanation: The 17 SDGs are to be achieved by 2030.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem: Which of the following situations shows a breach of the rule of law?
options: A court acquits an accused person for lack of evidence
A minister resigns after a scandal involving contracts in his ministry
The legislature passes the annual budget
A government ignores a court order to release a detained journalist
Citizens vote in a general election
questions.explanation: Disobedience of court orders by government undermines the supremacy of law.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem: How does good governance promote national development?
options: By increasing the number of public holidays
By preventing citizens from criticising leaders through the press and social media
By ensuring accountable use of resources for public welfare
By concentrating power in one person
questions.explanation: Accountable, transparent governance channels resources to development rather than waste or corruption.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem: Which of the following is an indicator that a country is developing?
options: Increase in literacy and life expectancy
Frequent collapse of buildings and bridges in the cities
questions.explanation: Rising literacy and life expectancy are signs of human development.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem: In a democracy, power is legitimately transferred from one government to another through
questions.explanation: Free and periodic elections are the democratic means of transferring power.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem: A citizen whose land is taken unlawfully by a governor can win his case in court. Which feature of democracy makes this possible?
questions.explanation: An independent judiciary protects rights and upholds the rule of law.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem: Corruption hinders national development mainly because it
options: increases the efficiency of public services
reduces the cost of public projects
diverts public funds meant for development into private pockets
questions.explanation: Corruption diverts resources, inflates costs and discourages investment.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem: Which of the following is a benefit of democracy to citizens?
options: Concentration of power in the army
questions.explanation: Democracy protects rights and allows citizens to choose and change their leaders.

questions.stem: A citizen who refuses to register as a voter because "politics is a dirty game" is showing
questions.explanation: Political apathy is lack of interest in political activities.

questions.stem: Of about 93 million registered voters in Nigeria's 2023 presidential election, only about 25 million voted. This mainly reflects
questions.explanation: Turnout of under one-third of registered voters shows widespread non-participation.

questions.stem: Which of the following can cause political apathy among citizens?
options: Free and fair elections conducted regularly by an independent electoral body
Failure of leaders to fulfil campaign promises
Respect for the rule of law
questions.explanation: Broken promises and bad governance make citizens lose interest in politics.

questions.stem: When elections are frequently marred by thuggery and violence, many citizens are likely to
options: join political parties in greater numbers
questions.explanation: Fear of violence discourages people from taking part in elections.

questions.stem: Political apathy may result in the election of
options: leaders chosen by the majority of citizens
leaders who are loved by all
questions.explanation: When most citizens stay away, a small number of voters, sometimes manipulated, decide who governs.

questions.stem: Which of the following measures is MOST likely to reduce political apathy among young Nigerians?
options: Sustained civic education and credible elections
Increasing the minimum age limit for voting to 30 years in all elections
Banning young people from political rallies
Reducing the number of polling units
Holding elections only once in ten years
questions.explanation: Voter education and elections whose results reflect votes cast restore confidence and encourage participation.

questions.stem: A woman says she will not vote because her vote "will be changed anyway". Her attitude is mainly caused by
options: satisfaction with the performance of the present government
ignorance of the date of the election
the high cost of transport only
her support for the ruling party
loss of confidence in the electoral process
questions.explanation: Belief that results are manipulated leads citizens to withdraw from voting.

questions.stem: In Ward 7, residents no longer attend town-hall meetings and most did not vote at the last council poll. The residents are displaying
questions.explanation: Avoiding all political activities, including voting and meetings, indicates apathy.

questions.stem: Lack of interest or concern in elections and other political activities by citizens is described as
questions.explanation: Political apathy is indifference or lack of interest in politics.

questions.stem: The introduction of technology such as BVAS and the result viewing portal (IReV) by INEC was partly aimed at
options: reducing the number of registered voters
replacing voting with opinion polls conducted by private research firms
increasing public confidence in the electoral process
extending the tenure of elected officers
questions.explanation: Transparency in accreditation and result transmission is meant to build trust and encourage participation.

questions.stem: Which of the following groups has historically faced cultural barriers that discourage political participation in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Cultural and religious norms, violence and cost of politics discourage many women from contesting elections.

questions.stem: Poverty contributes to political apathy because poor citizens
options: have too much free time for politics and attend every party meeting
are banned from voting by law
may be preoccupied with survival or sell their votes
do not need any public services
questions.explanation: Hunger and survival concerns reduce interest in politics and expose the poor to vote buying.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a way citizens can show interest in politics?
questions.explanation: Voting is the basic form of political participation.

questions.stem: Organisations outside government formed by citizens to pursue common interests, such as NGOs and professional bodies, make up
questions.explanation: Civil society is the space of voluntary organisations between the family and the state.

questions.stem: Which of the following organisations deploys observers to monitor elections in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Yiaga Africa is a civil society organisation that observes elections and promotes youth participation.

questions.stem: Attending a public hearing organised by a legislative committee on a bill is a form of
questions.explanation: Public hearings allow citizens to contribute directly to law-making.

questions.stem: The Nigerian Bar Association can be regarded as part of civil society because it
options: is a voluntary professional association outside government
is an arm of the executive and is headed by the Attorney-General of the Federation
questions.explanation: Professional associations are non-state voluntary organisations, hence part of civil society.

questions.stem: Civil society organisations contribute to good governance mainly by
options: contesting elections to form government at the federal and state levels
demanding accountability and transparency from government
questions.explanation: CSOs monitor government, advocate reforms and hold leaders accountable.

questions.stem: A major challenge faced by many civil society organisations in Nigeria is
options: excess government support that makes them richer than the ministries they monitor
dependence on foreign donors and inadequate funding
lack of any issues to address
questions.explanation: Funding difficulties, dependence on donors, harassment and internal weaknesses limit CSOs.

questions.stem: Sending a signed petition to a legislator about bad roads in a community is an example of
questions.explanation: Petitions are a legitimate way for citizens to participate in governance.

questions.stem: A community-based organisation is best described as a group that
options: is set up by the federal government to collect taxes
is formed by residents to address local needs
is a branch of an international bank
is a unit of the Nigerian Army
is a political party at ward level
questions.explanation: CBOs are formed by members of a community to tackle local problems.

questions.stem: Which of these bodies is a non-governmental workers’ organisation and therefore part of civil society?
questions.explanation: The NUT is a voluntary trade union outside government.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST explains why popular participation is important in a democracy?
options: It reduces the number of elections and the cost of conducting them
It weakens the voice of citizens
It removes the need for a constitution
It concentrates power in a few hands
It makes government responsive and legitimate
questions.explanation: When citizens participate, government reflects their wishes and enjoys greater legitimacy.

questions.stem: The Freedom of Information Act strengthens civil society mainly by
options: controlling the funds and bank accounts of all NGOs
questions.explanation: The FOI Act gives citizens and organisations the right to request information held by public institutions.

questions.stem: Peaceful protest is a legitimate form of participation because the 1999 Constitution guarantees the right to
options: own property anywhere in Nigeria without any restriction
questions.explanation: Section 40 guarantees freedom of peaceful assembly and association.

questions.stem: Labour unions such as the Nigeria Labour Congress influence government policy mainly through
options: winning seats in the Senate under their own registered party name
questions.explanation: Unions use negotiation, strikes and public advocacy to press their demands.

questions.stem: The public service is meant to serve
options: only members of the ruling party and their families and supporters
questions.explanation: Public servants serve the public impartially.

questions.stem: The anti-corruption agency set up to investigate economic and financial crimes such as money laundering and advance fee fraud is the
options: Code of Conduct Tribunal and Bureau acting together
questions.explanation: The EFCC investigates and prosecutes economic and financial crimes.

questions.stem: The Public Complaints Commission in Nigeria functions as
options: a court that tries murder and armed robbery cases in the states
an ombudsman that investigates complaints against public institutions
questions.explanation: The PCC investigates complaints of administrative injustice by public bodies and officials.

questions.stem: Under the Code of Conduct for Public Officers, a public officer is NOT allowed to
options: own a house in his home town or in the state capital where he works
maintain or operate a bank account outside Nigeria
questions.explanation: The Fifth Schedule of the Constitution forbids specified public officers from operating foreign bank accounts.

questions.stem: The payroll system introduced by the federal government to remove ghost workers from the public service is
questions.explanation: The Integrated Personnel and Payroll Information System helps eliminate ghost workers.

questions.stem: The Treasury Single Account policy promotes accountability in the public service mainly by
options: allowing each agency to keep many separate accounts in commercial banks of its choice
increasing the salaries of public servants
consolidating government revenues into one account at the Central Bank
questions.explanation: TSA ensures that government revenue is paid into a unified account, improving transparency and control.

questions.stem: A public officer approves a contract for a company owned by his wife without declaring his interest. He is guilty of
questions.explanation: A conflict of interest arises where private interest clashes with official duty.

questions.stem: SERVICOM was introduced in the Nigerian public service to
options: collect import duties at the seaports and airports
questions.explanation: SERVICOM (Service Compact with All Nigerians) aims to ensure efficient and courteous service delivery.

questions.stem: Which of the following qualities is expected of a public servant in a democracy?
questions.explanation: Public servants must be impartial and serve all citizens fairly.

questions.stem: The Code of Conduct Bureau requires public officers to
questions.explanation: Public officers must declare their assets on assumption and at the end of office.

questions.stem: Which of the following best explains why public servants should be politically neutral in a democracy?
options: So they can control election results in favour of the party they prefer
So they can serve any government faithfully
So they can avoid paying taxes
So they can become politicians easily
So they can ignore government policies
questions.explanation: Neutrality ensures continuity and loyal service whichever party wins.

questions.stem: The Federal Character Commission promotes fairness in the public service by
options: ensuring a fair spread of jobs among states
questions.explanation: The Commission monitors the distribution of public service posts among states and local governments.

questions.stem: The use of public office for private gain is
questions.explanation: Corruption is the abuse of public office for private benefit.

questions.stem: Spacing the births of children helps mainly to
options: protect the health of mother and child
questions.explanation: Adequate spacing allows the mother to recover and improves child survival.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a basic duty of parents to their children?
questions.explanation: Parents must provide basic needs such as food, shelter, clothing, health care and education.

questions.stem: Under the Child's Rights Act, the minimum age at which a person can validly marry is
questions.explanation: The Act prohibits marriage of persons below 18 years.

questions.stem: Parents who show their children love, set rules and also listen to their views are practising
questions.explanation: Balanced care, discipline and communication are features of responsible parenting.

questions.stem: A person who is accused of a crime is presumed to be
questions.explanation: Section 36(5) presumes every accused person innocent until proven guilty.

questions.stem: Which of the following courts is found at the lowest level of the state judicial system?
questions.explanation: Magistrate, district, area and customary courts are the lower courts in the states.

questions.stem: The Nigeria Police Force is established by section 214 of the 1999 Constitution as
options: a separate police force for each state under the control of its governor
a single police force for the whole Federation
questions.explanation: Section 214 provides that there shall be a Nigeria Police Force and no other police force for the Federation or any part of it.

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST explains why ignorance of the law is not an excuse?
options: Laws are published and every citizen is expected to know them
Only lawyers can break the law
Courts do not care about justice for those who are unaware of the law
Ignorance is a form of crime
questions.explanation: If ignorance were an excuse anyone could escape liability; citizens are expected to know published laws.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain five agents through which values are transmitted in society. [10 marks]
(b) State five consequences of the breakdown of values in Nigeria. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Family: parents teach children right conduct from birth
2 marks: School: teachers and school rules instil discipline and civic values
2 marks: Religious bodies: teach honesty, love and fear of God
2 marks: Peer groups: shape attitudes and behaviour of young people
2 marks: Mass media/government agencies such as the NOA: spread messages on acceptable conduct
1 mark: Corruption in public and private life
1 mark: Examination malpractice
1 mark: Increase in crime, cultism and drug abuse
1 mark: Disrespect for elders and constituted authority
1 mark: Get-rich-quick syndrome/internet fraud
questions.explanation: Values are passed on by the family, the school, religious institutions, peer groups, the mass media and agencies such as the National Orientation Agency. When values break down, society experiences corruption, examination malpractice, crime and cultism, drug abuse, disrespect for authority and a get-rich-quick mentality that despises honest work.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain five ways by which the government can promote national unity in Nigeria. [10 marks]
(b) State five duties of a good citizen to the nation. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Fair distribution of amenities and appointments (federal character)
2 marks: Programmes such as the NYSC and unity schools that bring youths from different areas together
2 marks: Promoting national symbols, sports and cultural festivals
2 marks: Good governance, justice and equal treatment of all groups
2 marks: Civic education and enlightenment through the NOA and the media
1 mark: Obeying the laws of the land
1 mark: Paying taxes
1 mark: Voting during elections
1 mark: Protecting public property
1 mark: Defending the country/respecting national symbols
questions.explanation: Government can foster unity through fairness in appointments and projects, unity schools and the NYSC, the promotion of national symbols, sports and festivals, good governance and justice to all groups, and public enlightenment. Citizens in turn should obey the law, pay taxes, vote, protect public property, respect national symbols and be ready to defend the country.

questions.stem:
(a) With an example in each case, distinguish between civil and political rights and economic, social and cultural rights. [6 marks]
(b) Explain three circumstances under which the 1999 Constitution allows fundamental rights to be restricted. [9 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Civil and political rights protect individual liberty and participation, e.g. right to life, fair hearing, vote
3 marks: Economic, social and cultural rights relate to welfare and well-being, e.g. right to education, health, work; largely non-justiciable in Nigeria (Chapter II)
3 marks: In the interest of defence, public safety, public order, public morality or public health (section 45)
3 marks: To protect the rights and freedoms of other persons (section 45)
3 marks: During a period of emergency, measures reasonably justifiable for dealing with the situation; also lawful sentence of a court or arrest on reasonable suspicion (sections 33, 35)
questions.explanation: Civil and political rights, such as the rights to life, liberty, fair hearing and voting, protect personal freedom and participation and are enforceable under Chapter IV. Economic, social and cultural rights, such as education, health and work, concern welfare and appear mainly in Chapter II, which the courts generally cannot enforce. The Constitution allows restrictions in the interest of defence, public safety, order, morality and health; to protect the rights of others; during an emergency; and in execution of court sentences or lawful arrest.

questions.stem:
(a) State three functions of the National Human Rights Commission. [6 marks]
(b) Explain three ways by which citizens can protect their fundamental rights. [9 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Receives and investigates complaints of human rights violations
2 marks: Promotes human rights awareness and education
2 marks: Assists victims to seek redress/monitors detention facilities and recommends remedies
3 marks: Going to court (High Court) to enforce rights under section 46
3 marks: Reporting violations to the NHRC, Public Complaints Commission, Legal Aid Council or civil society groups
3 marks: Knowing their rights and using the media or peaceful protest to draw attention to abuses
questions.explanation: The National Human Rights Commission, set up in 1995, investigates complaints of human rights abuses, educates the public, monitors places of detention, assists victims and recommends remedies. Citizens protect their rights by learning them, approaching the High Court under section 46, reporting abuses to the NHRC, the Public Complaints Commission, the Legal Aid Council or human rights organisations, and using the press and lawful protest.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain three types of law. [6 marks]
(b) Explain three agencies responsible for maintaining law and order in Nigeria and the role of each. [9 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Criminal law: deals with offences against the state, e.g. murder, theft
2 marks: Civil law: governs disputes between private persons, e.g. contracts, land
2 marks: Constitutional law/customary law/Islamic law (any other type correctly explained)
3 marks: Nigeria Police Force: prevents and detects crime, arrests offenders, maintains order
3 marks: Courts: try offenders and settle disputes
3 marks: Nigerian Correctional Service/NSCDC/FRSC: keeps and reforms offenders, protects infrastructure or enforces road rules (any one correctly explained)
questions.explanation: Criminal law punishes wrongs against society; civil law settles private disputes; constitutional law sets out the structure of government, while customary and Islamic laws apply in personal and community matters. Law and order are maintained by the police, who prevent and detect crime; the courts, which try cases; the Correctional Service, which keeps and rehabilitates offenders; and agencies such as the NSCDC and FRSC.

questions.stem:
(a) What is family planning? [3 marks]
(b) Explain four benefits of family planning to the family. [8 marks]
(c) State four consequences of irresponsible parenthood on society. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Family planning is the conscious decision by a couple on the number of children to have and the spacing between births
2 marks: Protects the health of mother and child
2 marks: Enables parents to provide adequately for each child
2 marks: Allows children to receive good education and attention
2 marks: Reduces financial strain and promotes family happiness
1 mark: Juvenile delinquency/crime
1 mark: Increase in street children and child hawking
1 mark: School drop-out and illiteracy
1 mark: Child trafficking/drug abuse among youths
questions.explanation: Family planning is deciding deliberately how many children to have and how far apart. It safeguards the health of mothers and children, lets parents meet each child's needs, supports good education and reduces financial pressure. Irresponsible parenthood breeds delinquency, street children and hawking, school drop-outs, trafficking and drug abuse.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of each of the following categories of road signs, giving one example of each: (i) warning signs (ii) regulatory signs (iii) informative signs. [9 marks]
(b) State three functions of the Federal Road Safety Corps. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Warning signs: usually triangular; alert road users to danger ahead, e.g. sharp bend, pedestrian crossing
3 marks: Regulatory signs: usually circular; give orders that must be obeyed, e.g. no entry, speed limit, stop
3 marks: Informative signs: usually rectangular; give information such as directions, distances, hospital
2 marks: Making highways safe for motorists and other road users
2 marks: Educating drivers and the public on road safety
2 marks: Issuing driver's licences and number plates/clearing obstructions and rescuing crash victims
questions.explanation: Warning signs, usually triangular, alert drivers to hazards such as bends or crossings. Regulatory signs, usually circular (and the octagonal stop sign), give mandatory or prohibitive orders such as no entry or speed limits. Informative signs, usually rectangular, give directions, distances and facilities. The FRSC makes highways safe, educates road users, designs and issues licences and number plates, removes obstructions and rescues crash victims.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain five methods of resolving conflicts in inter-personal relationships. [10 marks]
(b) State five causes of conflict between friends. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Dialogue: the parties discuss the issue openly
2 marks: Negotiation/compromise: each side gives up part of its demands
2 marks: Mediation: a neutral third party helps the parties reach agreement
2 marks: Arbitration: a third party hears both sides and gives a binding decision
2 marks: Reconciliation/apology and forgiveness
1 mark: Misunderstanding/poor communication
1 mark: Dishonesty or betrayal of trust
1 mark: Jealousy
1 mark: Gossip
1 mark: Failure to repay debts/selfishness
questions.explanation: Conflicts may be resolved by dialogue, negotiation and compromise, mediation by a neutral person, arbitration in which a third party decides, and reconciliation through apology and forgiveness. Causes of conflict between friends include misunderstanding, dishonesty, jealousy, gossip, selfishness and unpaid debts.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain five effects of cultism on educational institutions. [10 marks]
(b) State five measures the government can take to curb cultism. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Loss of lives of students and staff
2 marks: Disruption or closure of schools and the academic calendar
2 marks: Fear and insecurity on campus
2 marks: Fall in academic standards and examination malpractice
2 marks: Destruction of property/expulsion and wasted careers of students
1 mark: Enforcing anti-cult laws and prosecuting offenders
1 mark: Funding guidance and counselling units
1 mark: Public enlightenment campaigns
1 mark: Providing recreational and youth programmes
1 mark: Improving campus security
questions.explanation: Cultism leads to killings and injuries, closure of schools and disrupted calendars, fear and insecurity, falling standards and malpractice, destroyed property and ruined futures for expelled members. Government can curb it by enforcing anti-cult laws, prosecuting offenders, funding counselling, enlightening the public, providing alternative youth activities and improving security.

questions.stem:
(a) Name four classes of drugs and give one example of each. [8 marks]
(b) Explain the roles of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency in the fight against drug abuse. [7 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Stimulants, e.g. cocaine, amphetamine, caffeine
2 marks: Depressants, e.g. alcohol, barbiturates
2 marks: Narcotics/opioids, e.g. heroin, morphine, tramadol
2 marks: Hallucinogens, e.g. LSD, cannabis
2 marks: Arrests and prosecutes drug traffickers
2 marks: Seizes and destroys illicit drugs and farms
2 marks: Educates the public on the dangers of drug abuse
1 mark: Counsels and rehabilitates drug users/works with international agencies
questions.explanation: Drugs may be grouped as stimulants (cocaine, caffeine), depressants (alcohol, barbiturates), narcotics or opioids (heroin, tramadol) and hallucinogens (LSD, cannabis). The NDLEA, established in 1989, arrests and prosecutes traffickers, seizes drugs and destroys cannabis farms, runs public enlightenment campaigns, refers users for counselling and rehabilitation, and cooperates with international agencies.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain five forms of human trafficking. [10 marks]
(b) State five functions of the National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons (NAPTIP). [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Sexual exploitation/forced prostitution
2 marks: Forced labour, e.g. on farms or in mines
2 marks: Domestic servitude/child labour as house helps
2 marks: Organ harvesting
2 marks: Child soldiers, forced begging or baby trafficking
1 mark: Investigates and prosecutes traffickers
1 mark: Rescues victims
1 mark: Rehabilitates and counsels victims
1 mark: Creates public awareness
1 mark: Cooperates with foreign agencies/enforces the anti-trafficking law
questions.explanation: Trafficking takes forms such as sexual exploitation, forced labour, domestic servitude, organ harvesting and the use of children as soldiers or beggars, and the sale of babies. NAPTIP investigates and prosecutes traffickers, rescues, shelters and rehabilitates victims, runs awareness campaigns, enforces the anti-trafficking law and cooperates with international partners.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain five ways of preventing the spread of HIV. [10 marks]
(b) State five ways in which society should treat people living with HIV. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Abstinence from sex/being faithful to one uninfected partner
2 marks: Correct and consistent use of condoms
2 marks: Use of sterilised needles, razors and sharp objects
2 marks: Screening of blood before transfusion
2 marks: Prevention of mother-to-child transmission through testing and antiretroviral drugs
1 mark: Show love and care
1 mark: Avoid stigmatisation and discrimination
1 mark: Encourage them to take their drugs
1 mark: Keep their status confidential
1 mark: Give them equal access to jobs and education
questions.explanation: HIV spread can be prevented by abstinence and faithfulness, condom use, avoiding shared sharp objects, screening blood, and testing and treating pregnant women. People living with HIV should be treated with love, without stigma or discrimination, supported to stay on treatment, have their status kept confidential and be given equal opportunities.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain five government programmes or agencies for youth empowerment in Nigeria. [10 marks]
(b) State five challenges facing youth empowerment programmes in Nigeria. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: National Directorate of Employment (NDE): vocational training and job creation
2 marks: SMEDAN: support for small businesses
2 marks: N-Power: engagement and training of unemployed youths
2 marks: NYSC SAED: skills and entrepreneurship for corps members
2 marks: NELFUND/Industrial Training Fund/Bank of Industry youth schemes (any valid one)
1 mark: Inadequate funding
1 mark: Corruption
1 mark: Political interference in selection of beneficiaries
1 mark: Poor monitoring and continuity
1 mark: Lack of access to credit and infrastructure
questions.explanation: Programmes include the NDE (vocational training), SMEDAN (support for small enterprises), N-Power (job placement and training), NYSC SAED (skills for corps members), NELFUND (student loans) and the ITF. They are hampered by poor funding, corruption, political selection of beneficiaries, weak monitoring, discontinuity and lack of credit and power supply.

questions.stem:
(a) Describe the structure of a local government council in Nigeria. [5 marks]
(b) Explain five functions of local governments in Nigeria. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Executive arm headed by an elected chairman (with a vice-chairman, secretary and supervisory councillors)
2 marks: Legislative arm made up of elected councillors representing wards, headed by a leader of the council
1 mark: Administrative staff/departments headed by career officers
2 marks: Collection of rates and taxes
2 marks: Establishment and maintenance of markets and motor parks
2 marks: Registration of births, deaths and marriages
2 marks: Provision of primary health care and primary education support
2 marks: Construction of rural roads/naming of streets/refuse disposal
questions.explanation: A local government council has an executive led by an elected chairman, with a vice-chairman, secretary and supervisory councillors; a legislative arm of elected ward councillors; and administrative departments of career staff. Its functions include collecting rates, managing markets and motor parks, registering births, deaths and marriages, primary health care, rural roads, street naming and sanitation.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem:
(a) Explain three principles of the rule of law. [9 marks]
(b) State three factors that hinder national development in Nigeria. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Supremacy of the law: everyone, including government, is subject to the law
3 marks: Equality before the law: same law applies to all irrespective of status
3 marks: Protection of fundamental rights/fair hearing by independent courts
2 marks: Corruption
2 marks: Insecurity and conflicts
2 marks: Poor infrastructure/bad leadership/unemployment
questions.explanation: The rule of law rests on the supremacy of law over arbitrary power, equality of all persons before the law, and the protection of rights through fair hearing before independent courts. National development is hindered by corruption, insecurity, poor leadership, inadequate infrastructure and unemployment.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem:
(a) Distinguish between direct democracy and representative democracy. [5 marks]
(b) Explain five ways in which democracy can promote national development. [10 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Direct democracy: citizens personally take part in making decisions, e.g. ancient Athens
2 marks: Representative democracy: citizens elect representatives who make decisions on their behalf
1 mark: Direct democracy suits small communities; representative suits large modern states
2 marks: Accountability of leaders reduces waste and corruption
2 marks: Protection of rights encourages creativity and investment
2 marks: Peaceful change of government ensures stability
2 marks: Participation makes policies reflect people's needs
2 marks: Free press and rule of law attract foreign investment
questions.explanation: In direct democracy citizens themselves make decisions, as in ancient Athens or small village assemblies; in representative democracy they elect others to decide for them, which suits large states. Democracy aids development by making leaders accountable, protecting rights and property, ensuring peaceful transfers of power, involving citizens in policy and creating a stable climate for investment.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain five consequences of political apathy in a democracy. [10 marks]
(b) State five ways by which government can reduce political apathy. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Emergence of bad or incompetent leaders
2 marks: Weak legitimacy of elected governments
2 marks: Easier rigging and manipulation of elections
2 marks: Policies that do not reflect the wishes of the majority
2 marks: Weakening of democracy and possible return of authoritarian rule
1 mark: Conduct credible elections
1 mark: Civic and voter education
1 mark: Fulfilling campaign promises/good governance
1 mark: Ending electoral violence
1 mark: Making registration and voting easier
questions.explanation: Apathy allows poor leaders to emerge, weakens the legitimacy of governments chosen by few voters, makes rigging easier, produces policies that ignore the majority and endangers democracy itself. Government can respond with credible elections, civic education, good governance, security during elections and easier registration and voting.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain five forms of popular participation in governance. [10 marks]
(b) State five challenges facing civil society organisations in Nigeria. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Voting in elections
2 marks: Joining political parties and contesting elections
2 marks: Attending public hearings and town-hall meetings
2 marks: Writing petitions/letters to representatives
2 marks: Peaceful protest and membership of pressure groups/CSOs
1 mark: Inadequate funding
1 mark: Government harassment and restrictive laws
1 mark: Dependence on foreign donors
1 mark: Internal disunity and poor management
1 mark: Low public awareness/partisan capture
questions.explanation: Citizens participate by voting, joining parties and contesting, attending public hearings and town-hall meetings, petitioning representatives, joining civil society groups and protesting peacefully. CSOs face poor funding, harassment, dependence on donors, internal disunity, low public awareness and attempts by politicians to co-opt them.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain three anti-corruption agencies in Nigeria and the role of each. [9 marks]
(b) State three ways of making the public service more efficient. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: EFCC: investigates and prosecutes economic and financial crimes such as money laundering and fraud
3 marks: ICPC: investigates corrupt practices in public offices and educates against corruption
3 marks: Code of Conduct Bureau/Tribunal: receives asset declarations and tries breaches of the Code of Conduct
2 marks: Recruitment and promotion based on merit
2 marks: Regular training and better pay
2 marks: Use of technology (e.g. IPPIS) and enforcement of discipline
questions.explanation: The EFCC handles economic and financial crimes; the ICPC deals with corruption in public institutions and runs prevention and education; the Code of Conduct Bureau receives asset declarations and the Code of Conduct Tribunal tries public officers who breach the Code. Efficiency improves through merit-based recruitment, training, adequate pay, technology such as IPPIS and firm discipline.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain three provisions of the Code of Conduct for Public Officers in the 1999 Constitution. [9 marks]
(b) Explain two reasons why public officers should be accountable to the people. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Public officers must not put themselves in positions where personal interest conflicts with their duties
3 marks: They must declare their assets on assumption of office, periodically and at the end of tenure
3 marks: Specified officers must not maintain foreign bank accounts or accept gifts/bribes for their duties
3 marks: They manage public resources held in trust for the people
3 marks: Accountability reduces corruption and builds public trust/legitimacy
questions.explanation: The Fifth Schedule forbids conflicts of interest, requires declaration of assets on assumption of office, every four years and at the end of tenure, and bars specified officers from operating foreign accounts or accepting bribes or improper gifts. Officers must be accountable because they hold public resources in trust for the people, and accountability reduces corruption and builds confidence in government.
